title: Two verification loops
summary: Focused development checks and candidate release gates serve different purposes.

sections.label: Recommended practice
sections.text: Use quick checks for the change in progress and broader gates for the candidate being reviewed. Define what each loop must prove before choosing its checks.

sections.label: Project adaptation
sections.text: Use relevant unit, integration, query, and interface checks while developing. Apply your project's established CI, quality, and release gates at the appropriate milestone. Jenkins and Sonar are examples.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Do not run every expensive gate after every edit, and do not treat one focused check as sufficient release evidence.

sections.label: Example source: Talos work-test cycle
sections.text: The inspected Talos runbook describes a focused inner loop for small changes and a heavier Release QA Gate for candidate evidence tied to the exact SHA. This is a finding about the reviewed contents, not a verified execution result.

confidence: Moderate for adaptation. High for inspected runbook contents
